title: Sixth Word The Two Mens Responses And Outcomes

questions.question: In the comparison, what did the king give to each of the two men?
questions.answer: He placed each man in charge of an estate with the equipment and supplies needed to run it.

questions.question: What was the condition of the time they were living in?
questions.answer: It was a dangerous time full of unrest and war, so nothing stayed secure.

questions.question: Why did the king ask the two men to hand over the property to him?
questions.answer: He wanted to protect it from being wasted or destroyed and return it later in better condition.

questions.question: What did the king promise to do after the wars ended?
questions.answer: He promised to give the property back in an improved form.

questions.question: How did the king say he would treat the trust in the meantime?
questions.answer: He said he would count it as if it were their own property and pay them generously for it.

questions.question: What did the king promise about the tools and machines?
questions.answer: He said they would be used in his service and that their return and payment would become far greater.

questions.question: Why did the king say the men should let him handle the costs of the work?
questions.answer: Because they were poor and unable to cover such large expenses on their own.

questions.question: What are two benefits the king mentioned if they accepted his offer?
questions.answer: He would cover the expenses, and they would still receive the gains and profits.

questions.question: What warning did the king give if they refused to sell the property back to him?
questions.answer: They would fail to keep it safe, lose it without benefit, and miss the high reward.

questions.question: Besides losing the estate, what would happen to the valuable tools and materials if they refused?
questions.answer: Those precious things would lose their worth.

questions.question: What extra burden would fall on the men if they rejected the king’s offer?
questions.answer: They would carry the stress of managing and guarding the property and also face punishment for breaking trust.

questions.question: What new rank would a man receive if he accepted the king’s offer?
questions.answer: He would become the king’s soldier and a trusted officer instead of a low, ordinary fighter.

questions.question: How did the wiser of the two men respond to the message?
questions.answer: He gladly accepted it and was thankful.

questions.question: What kind of character did the other man show?
questions.answer: He showed pride, selfishness, and careless love of pleasure.

questions.question: What false idea led the second man to reject the king’s offer?
questions.answer: He acted as if he would remain on the estate forever.

questions.question: What happened to the first man after some time?
questions.answer: He rose to a high position, gained the king’s favor, and lived in comfort.

questions.question: What happened to the second man after some time?
questions.answer: He lost his happiness and property and ended up in punishment and suffering.

questions.question: Who carried the king’s message to the two men?
questions.answer: A noble representative sent by the king.

questions.question: What does the king’s message show about his attitude toward the two men?
questions.answer: It shows mercy, care, and a desire to help them.

questions.question: Why was the property not safe in their hands forever?
questions.answer: Because the world around them was unstable and likely to bring loss or change.

questions.question: What did the king ask them to do with the property they were holding?
questions.answer: He asked them to return it to him by selling it back to him.

questions.question: According to the message, how would the king prevent the property from being wasted?
questions.answer: He would keep and protect it himself until the troubled time was over.

questions.question: What did the king promise concerning payment?
questions.answer: He promised a great payment for the property.

questions.question: How would using the tools in the king’s service benefit the men?
questions.answer: Their use would bring much greater payment and gain than before.

questions.question: What does the king’s offer suggest about the men’s ability to manage everything alone?
questions.answer: It suggests they were too limited and needy to manage such heavy responsibilities by themselves.

questions.question: What does the phrase about demobilization mean in this comparison?
questions.answer: It means there would come a later time when the period of struggle would end.

questions.question: Why was refusing the offer a bad choice even from a practical point of view?
questions.answer: Because they could not truly keep the property anyway, so refusal would only end in loss.

questions.question: What five kinds of harm are mentioned in a general way for refusal?
questions.answer: Loss of the property, loss of the offered payment, loss of value in the tools, the burden of guarding them, and punishment for betrayal.

questions.question: How would the man’s social and military position improve if he agreed?
questions.answer: He would no longer be treated like a common captive or irregular fighter but as a free and honored officer.

questions.question: Which of the two men made the wiser decision?
questions.answer: The one who accepted with gratitude.

questions.question: What inner weakness seems to control the second man?
questions.answer: His ego and pride control him.

questions.question: How does the passage show that the second man misunderstood reality?
questions.answer: He ignored the disasters and acted like his enjoyment would never end.

questions.question: What was the final outcome for the grateful man?
questions.answer: He reached honor, earned favor, and lived happily close to the king.

questions.question: What was the final outcome for the arrogant man?
questions.answer: He fell into misery, lost what he had, and suffered for his mistake.

questions.question: What important choice was placed before the two men?
questions.answer: They had to choose whether to trust the king and hand over the estate or keep clinging to it themselves.

questions.question: Why does the king’s request not count as unfair taking?
questions.answer: Because the property was already being held in trust, and he offered protection and reward in return.

questions.question: What does the unstable setting add to the meaning of the story?
questions.answer: It shows that worldly possessions are not secure and can disappear quickly.

questions.question: What did the king offer instead of mere protection?
questions.answer: He offered protection, improvement, payment, and honor.

questions.question: How does the king’s promise about increased payment for the tools raise the value of obedience?
questions.answer: It shows that serving under the king turns ordinary work into something far more rewarding.

questions.question: What does the message tell us about the men’s financial condition?
questions.answer: They were poor and unable to handle major costs by themselves.

questions.question: Why would the men still profit even though the king would take over the expenses?
questions.answer: Because he promised to let them keep the income and gain.

questions.question: What kind of reasoning did the king use to persuade them?
questions.answer: He used both mercy and clear logic about gain and loss.

questions.question: Why is the first man called more intelligent?
questions.answer: Because he recognized the truth of the offer and chose what would truly benefit him.

questions.question: What personal qualities made the second man reject the offer?
questions.answer: Pride, selfishness, and living for pleasure.

questions.question: What mistake did the second man make about time and life on the estate?
questions.answer: He imagined his stay there would last forever.

questions.question: What happened to the first man’s rank, and what does that show?
questions.answer: His rank rose very high, showing that trust and obedience lead to elevation.

questions.question: Why did people both pity the second man and say he deserved his condition?
questions.answer: They felt sorry for his suffering, but they knew it came from his own bad choice.

questions.question: What did the second man lose besides material property?
questions.answer: He also lost happiness.

questions.question: What role does free choice play in the story?
questions.answer: Each man chooses his path, and each one receives the result of his own decision.

questions.question: In simple words, what was the king offering the two men?
questions.answer: He was offering to protect what they had, reward them for it, and raise their status.

questions.question: Why did the king say the property might not last?
questions.answer: Because the time was full of conflict and change.

questions.question: What does it mean that the men were holding the property in trust?
questions.answer: It means they were caretakers, not absolute owners.

questions.question: What future hope did the king give them about the estate?
questions.answer: He promised it would come back to them in better shape later.

questions.question: What did the king say about the workshop items being used in his name?
questions.answer: He said using them for him would greatly increase their return.

questions.question: Why is the king’s offer especially kind considering the men’s condition?
questions.answer: Because they lacked the means to support the work themselves, yet he would cover the costs.

questions.question: What does the king’s speech teach about short-term effort and long-term reward?
questions.answer: Giving something up now for the right reason can bring a much greater reward later.

questions.question: If the men refused, what would happen to the precious items waiting to be used?
questions.answer: They would lose their worth.

questions.question: What emotional burden would come with refusing the offer?
questions.answer: Worry and stress over protecting what could not truly be kept.

questions.question: What legal or moral burden would also come with refusal?
questions.answer: Punishment for failing the trust.

questions.question: How did the king describe the new role of the one who accepted?
questions.answer: As an honored soldier serving under the king’s authority.

questions.question: Which response shows humility, and which shows arrogance?
questions.answer: The thankful acceptance shows humility, while the refusal shows arrogance.

questions.question: What does the first man’s gratitude tell us about his heart?
questions.answer: He was wise, humble, and able to appreciate mercy.

questions.question: What does the second man’s love of enjoyment do to his judgment?
questions.answer: It blinds him to danger and makes him choose badly.

questions.question: How is the second man’s downfall connected to his earlier attitude?
questions.answer: His suffering grows directly out of his proud refusal.

questions.question: What is the contrast between the final homes of the two men?
questions.answer: One lives happily in the king’s palace, while the other falls into misery and punishment.

questions.question: Why did others envy the first man?
questions.answer: Because he reached honor, favor, and a good life.

questions.question: What had the king placed under the care of each of the two subjects?
questions.answer: A full estate with useful working equipment and supplies.

questions.question: What danger threatened these estates?
questions.answer: The unstable and war-filled conditions made destruction or change very likely.

questions.question: How did the king communicate his offer?
questions.answer: He sent a respected officer with a merciful command.

questions.question: What was the main action the king asked from the two men?
questions.answer: He asked them to transfer the trust back to him.

questions.question: What reason did the king give for asking this from them?
questions.answer: He wanted to preserve it and keep it from being ruined for nothing.

questions.question: What improvement did the king promise in the future?
questions.answer: He said the property would be returned in a better state after the troubled period.

questions.question: What did the king promise concerning the earnings from the equipment?
questions.answer: He promised greatly multiplied returns and profits.

questions.question: Why would it help the men for the king to provide expenses and equipment?
questions.answer: Because they were unable to meet those demands on their own.

questions.question: What shows that the king’s offer included both generosity and authority?
questions.answer: He offered large benefits, but he also warned them of punishment if they betrayed the trust.

questions.question: Why could the men not simply keep everything safely by themselves?
questions.answer: Because no one had the power to hold onto such things permanently in that troubled time.

questions.question: What better identity would come to the man who accepted the offer?
questions.answer: He would serve as a free officer under a great ruler.

questions.question: What was the first man’s immediate reaction?
questions.answer: He accepted gladly and gave abundant thanks.

questions.question: How is the second man’s ego described through comparison?
questions.answer: His pride is shown as being extremely inflated and rebellious.

questions.question: What reality of the world did the second man ignore?
questions.answer: He ignored the disasters and shakings that prove life is not stable.

questions.question: How did the king reward the first man in the end?
questions.answer: He raised him in rank, favored him, and gave him a happy life in the palace.

questions.question: What did the second man experience in the end?
questions.answer: He was left with loss, punishment, and suffering.

questions.question: What lesson about trust can be learned from the different endings?
questions.answer: When a trust is handled faithfully, it leads to honor, but betraying it leads to loss.

questions.question: How many men are at the center of this parable, and what did they have in common at the start?
questions.answer: Two men, and both were entrusted with similar estates and equipment.

questions.question: What kind of world is described around them?
questions.answer: A world of instability, conflict, and constant change.

questions.question: Why is instability important to the king’s argument?
questions.answer: It proves that what they hold can easily be lost if left as it is.

questions.question: What did the king want to do for the property if the men agreed?
questions.answer: He wanted to guard it for them and later return it improved.

questions.question: What does the king’s promise of a high payment show?
questions.answer: It shows that giving back the trust would not leave them empty; it would reward them.

questions.question: How would the men’s tools become more beneficial under the king’s authority?
questions.answer: Their work would gain a far greater return than before.

questions.question: What problem of the men did the king promise to solve by taking on the expenses?
questions.answer: Their lack of resources and inability to handle the costs.

questions.question: What would happen if they refused and tried to keep control for themselves?
questions.answer: They would still lose the property and also lose the reward.

questions.question: What would happen to the valuable instruments if they were not used as the king directed?
questions.answer: Their value would fade away.

questions.question: Why would refusal bring punishment, not just loss?
questions.answer: Because refusing would amount to failing the trust placed in them.

questions.question: What honorable change of role was offered to the one who accepted?
questions.answer: He would become a trusted servant-soldier of the king with freedom and dignity.

questions.question: Which man showed real understanding of the situation?
questions.answer: The first man who accepted the offer.

questions.question: What does the second man’s behavior reveal about his character?
questions.answer: He is proud, self-centered, and attached to temporary pleasure.

questions.question: How does the passage connect arrogance with foolishness?
questions.answer: The arrogant man ignores clear danger and turns away from a generous offer that would save him.

questions.question: What was the long-term result of wisdom and thankfulness?
questions.answer: High rank, royal favor, and happy living.

questions.question: What was the long-term result of ego and refusal?
questions.answer: Loss, humiliation, and painful punishment.
